messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observed partial degradation during maintenance window - request for uptime recalculation

Hi Kimberly,

We observed a sustained increase in tail latency and a 5-8% error rise for our inference route (region: us-west-2) between 2027-08-14 02:45 - 03:30 UTC. Acme runs internal probes and I’ve attached our probe CSV for that window.

EdgeNet (our CDN provider) flagged a planned maintenance at 2027-08-13 23:50 UTC that they say affected some edge adapters, and I see Redwood had a short maintenance notice at 2027-08-14 02:30 UTC. Because these overlap, our billing and SLO calculation is showing minimal to no credit. From our perspective, this was a partial-path impact and should be excluded or at least apportioned differently — the user impact was measurable.

Could you explain the exact logic you used to decide not to apply a maintenance exclusion? We need the calculation breakdown (probes counted, window attribution, and whether third-party announcements were considered) to evaluate next steps on our end.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Health

Hi Samir — thanks for the note and the CSV. We definitely want to make sure the SLO accounting is fair. I’ve looped in Marissa from SRE and Ben from your account team so we can triage quickly.

To speed things up, please confirm the following so our reconciliation is apples-to-apples:
- Which route/endpoint and model variant were you using (URL or route id)?
- Are the probe IDs in the CSV synthetic probes from your infra or from a third-party vantage?
- Do you have a copy of the EdgeNet maintenance notice? (if you don’t, we can request it from EdgeNet)

Initial notes on our side: Redwood’s default maintenance exclusion requires (a) an overlapping scheduled maintenance on our side, or (b) a verified upstream provider outage that materially interrupts probe coverage. If neither condition is satisfied, we typically treat partial degradations as service degradations rather than full maintenance exclusions. That said, overlapping windows plus evidence of probe dropouts can change the calculation.

We’ll review the CSV and the EdgeNet notice when you send it, and we’ll produce a breakdown showing which probes/timestamps were included/excluded and the resulting uptime tally. Expect a first-pass by end of day tomorrow (08/15).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Support Escalations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-18T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: initial reconciliation notes for Acme - partial-path vs maintenance-chain

Kim / Ben,

I pulled the probe set and ran it against our edge logs for the 02:30-03:30 UTC window. Key findings:
- The error spike correlates to increased 5xxs from a subset of our gateway nodes (gw-08a, gw-08b) starting ~02:47 UTC.
- EdgeNet’s maint notice is targeted at edge adapters; their telemetry shows intermittent packet drops for ~18 minutes overlapping our window.
- Our scheduled maintenance (internal config refresh) was a brief rolling job with node-level restarts from 02:28-02:35 UTC; the bulk of customer-visible errors happened after that period.

Interpretation: this looks like a chained event — brief internal maintenance followed by degraded connectivity at the upstream adapter (EdgeNet). Because the majority of customer impact happened after our internal restart window, our standard stance would be to treat the period as a partial degradation influenced by third-party network behavior rather than a pure Redwood maintenance exclusion.

Proposal (to close with Acme):
- Offer a 25% pro-rata credit for the affected minute-range (02:47-03:05 UTC) while we continue deeper log reconciliation. Rationale: acknowledges customer impact, reflects shared responsibility since EdgeNet shows packet loss, and preserves policy consistency.
- Commit to 72-hour follow-up after SRE completes kernel trace and we get any post-fact EdgeNet audit logs.

I attached a short recalc workbook (recalc-sheet-kp-20270818.xlsx) with the probe inclusion/exclusion list and the credit math. If you’re comfortable with the 25% proposal, Ben can present it to Samir; we can escalate to Legal if Acme pushes for a full exclusion.

-Marissa
